page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.6xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance built on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz, it features 12 physical cores and 24 virtual vCPUs via two threads per core. The system is configured with 48.0 GB of RAM, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. System cache resources include 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 35 MB shared L3 cache. Instruction set support includes AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and FMA. No local ephemeral disk storage is bundled with this instance, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 8 Gbps.

Performance benchmarking places the instance within the average category for multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth, while single-core metrics fall into lower performance brackets. Multi-core performance reaches a stress-ng score of 21007.3 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8967.0. Memory read bandwidth measured 108.94 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, with write throughput recorded at 47.99 GB/sec. In application-specific testing, the server demonstrated 20.09 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 15.86 GB/sec in static web serving. Single-core CPU stress-ng testing scored 1313.3, and single-threaded gzip compression registered 22.86 GB/sec.

Providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.c6.6xlarge balances core count and memory allocation for parallel execution without paying for excess RAM capacity. The key trade-offs include lower single-threaded performance compared to newer architecture generations and complete reliance on external block storage due to the absence of local disks. This hardware profile makes the instance suitable for parallelized software builds, CI/CD execution, web server clusters, and multi-threaded batch data processing.
